security_spec.violation_condition: In OpenSBI M-mode interrupt trap handler, when the hardware (via Smivt IVT mode) automatically clears the interrupt-pending bit before the firmware handler executes, any firmware code that reads the pending register (e.g., mip, sip, or ACLIC interrupt-pending registers) to identify the interrupt source will observe already-cleared bits, losing information about which interrupt triggered the trap—especially for edge-triggered interrupts where clearing is guaranteed.
security_spec.summary: Smivt IVT mode hardware now auto-clears interrupt-pending bits on trap entry; OpenSBI M-mode handlers that read pending registers after trap entry to identify the interrupt source will see stale/zero bits on edge-triggered interrupts, causing interrupt source loss and unhandled interrupts.

findings.finding: Interrupt source identification uses mcause exception code (line 322: mcause & ~MCAUSE_IRQ_MASK) for non-AIA interrupts and CSR_MTOPI (line 261: csr_read(CSR_MTOPI)) for AIA interrupts. Neither path reads mip/sip pending registers to identify the interrupt source. Under Smivt IVT mode, hardware clearing of pending bits would not cause loss of interrupt source information.

spec_citations.excerpt: If the fetch is successful, the hart clears the low bit(s) (depending on IALIGN) of the handler address, clears the corresponding interrupt-pending bit if possible, and sets the PC to this handler address.

findings.finding: Non-AIA interrupt dispatch switches on the IRQ code extracted from mcause, not on pending register bits. The switch cases (IRQ_M_TIMER, IRQ_M_SOFT, IRQ_M_EXT) are driven by the trap cause, not by polling mip/sip.

AIA interrupt dispatch reads CSR_MTOPI (the AIA top-priority-interrupt CSR) in a while loop, which provides the interrupt identity directly. This does not rely on pending bit registers (mip/sip) for source identification.
Assembly trap entry saves mcause into the trap context via TRAP_SAVE_INFO macro (line 680) and passes it to sbi_trap_handler. No read of mip/sip pending registers is performed in the trap entry path.

HSM suspend saves mip bits (MIP_SSIP | MIP_STIP) for non-retentive suspend. This is a suspend/resume save-restore operation, not an interrupt source identification in a trap handler — it correctly filters only the S-mode writable bits.

PMU code reads mip only to check the PMU overflow interrupt (MIP_PMOVI) status before clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent. This is a race-condition guard for PMU overflow handling, not interrupt source identification in a trap handler. It correctly guards against premature clearing of the overflow flag.

Platform-specific PMU code reads mip only to check PMU overflow interrupt status before clearing MCOUNTEROVF. Same PMU race-condition guard pattern, not interrupt source identification in a trap handler.
